facts.fact_text: On 18 March 2003, the applicant, Mr Sh., and Ms M. sent a notice to the head of Yekaterinburg town administration of their intention to stage a picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
The declared purpose of the picket was 'to attract public attention to violations of the human right of access to a court'.
On 25 March 2003, the applicant and others held the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others distributed press clippings and leaflets about Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court, who had allegedly been involved in corruption scandals.
During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others collected signatures for the dismissal of Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.

In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers committed an administrative offence by violating section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council of 28 July 1988, as amended by the Presidential Decree of 25 May 1992.

In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that pursuant to section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council of 28 July 1988, Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. were administratively liable under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The justice of the peace declared the applicant guilty under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The justice of the peace fined the applicant 1,000 Russian roubles (approximately 35 euros).
The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 was in force at the material time pursuant to Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992.

Under section 2 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to give written notice to the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly.

Under section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, assemblies were to be conducted in accordance with the aims listed in the notice and with respect for Soviet laws and public order.

Under section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, individuals who breached the established procedure for organising and holding assemblies incurred liability under the laws of the USSR and Soviet republics.

Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that a breach of the established procedure for organising a demonstration, meeting, procession or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum monthly wage, which was 1,000 to 2,000 Russian roubles at the material time.

Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences stipulates that a breach of the established procedure for holding a demonstration, meeting or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum wage for organisers, or five to ten times the minimum wage for participants.
The declared purpose of the picket was 'to attract public attention to violations of the human right of access to a court'.

Under section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, assemblies were to be conducted in accordance with the aims listed in the notice and with respect for Soviet laws and public order.
In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers misled the officials of the Yekaterinburg town administration as to the real purposes of their action.

In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that instead of drawing public attention to the problems of judicial protection and violations of human rights as indicated in the picket notice, for three days the picket participants distributed printed leaflets and materials of a slanderous and insulting nature which targeted the president of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court personally.
In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the information contained in the extract from the Novaya Gazeta newspaper was more than two years old.

In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the information in the Novaya Gazeta newspaper extract had been checked by the Supreme Qualification Panel of Judges and the Prosecutor General's Office and found to be slanderous.

In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket participants, in particular Mr Sh. and Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), were perfectly aware that the information in the Novaya Gazeta newspaper extract had been found to be slanderous.
In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers deliberately and maliciously changed the nature of the action and thereby misled the public.
The justice of the peace found that the picket had been conducted at variance with the aims listed in the notice.

The picket participants distributed extracts from the Novaya Gazeta newspaper containing A. Politkovskaya's article 'Ovcharuk and his team', which in its contents did not correspond to the aims of the picket as stated in the notice.
